# inspectrum

**Offline visualiser for captured radio signals — read a waveform by eye**

- **Version recorded:** 0.3.1
- **Categories:** `signal-analysis`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/miek/inspectrum>

## What it does

Opens a recorded IQ capture and displays it as a spectrogram you can zoom, measure and annotate, with cursors for reading off symbol rates and decoding simple modulation by hand.

## Why you would want it

It is how you work out what an unknown signal is before writing any code to decode it. Nothing else makes the structure of a capture -- preamble, symbol period, modulation -- as immediately visible, and it is entirely offline, so it needs no hardware at all.

## Before it will work

A recorded IQ file. Nothing transmits and no receiver is required, which makes it a good first tool for someone who owns no hardware yet.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profiles:** [`rf-security`](../profiles/rf-security.md), [`sdr`](../profiles/sdr.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install inspectrum --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `inspectrum`

## Known problems

Large captures are memory-hungry; a multi-gigabyte recording will struggle. It reads raw IQ and expects you to know the sample format and rate of the file, which is not stored in a bare .cfile.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
